summary:
MISSIONVARIESSI: Interactive Lunar and Mars Mission Simulator
MissionVariessi is an interactive space mission simulation platform developed by HONGIE MIGUEL TEAM to help users explore, plan and simulate lunar and Mars exploration missions. The platform allows users to configure missions, select crew sizes, adjust available power, set mission durations and simulate challenging scenarios such as solar storms, communication failures, power-system faults and surface hazards.
By transforming complex mission conditions into visual simulations, timelines and risk assessments, MissionVariessi helps users understand how unexpected events can affect mission operations and how alternative decisions may improve preparedness.
Our project addresses the challenge of making space mission planning and decision-making more accessible, interactive and understandable. It provides an educational environment where students, researchers and space enthusiasts can experiment with mission scenarios without affecting real spacecraft or astronauts.
MissionVariessi is important because future lunar and Mars exploration will require careful planning, effective resource management and the ability to respond to unexpected challenges. Our vision is to make space exploration more accessible through simulation, technology and intelligent decision support.
details: MISSIONVARIESSI Interactive Lunar and Mars Mission Simulation Platform Team: HONGIE MIGUEL TEAM | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 MissionVariessi is an innovative space exploration simulation platform designed to allow users to plan, simulate and analyse hypothetical missions to the Moon and Mars. The platform provides an interactive environment where students, researchers and space enthusiasts can experience the challenges of space exploration without travelling beyond Earth. Users can select between lunar and Martian missions, establish mission objectives, allocate resources and explore different operational scenarios. The platform focuses on important mission factors such as fuel consumption, oxygen supply, water availability, energy management, communication delays, radiation exposure and astronaut safety. One of its key features is the Mission Scenario Simulator, which allows users to explore unexpected situations, including spacecraft malfunctions, communication failures, solar storms and limited resources. Users can examine how these challenges affect mission operations and explore possible solutions. Through interactive visualisation and simulation, MissionVariessi transforms theoretical space education into practical learning. The project offers several benefits. It improves understanding of astronomy, planetary science and spacecraft operations while encouraging critical thinking, creativity and problem-solving. It also introduces users to resource management, mission planning and risk assessment. Most importantly, it makes space science more accessible to young people, particularly students who have limited access to advanced scientific facilities. Our intended impact is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, researchers and astronauts. MissionVariessi aims to promote STEM education, increase awareness of lunar and Martian exploration and encourage African participation in global space innovation. In the long term, we envision an accessible educational platform that supports scientific experimentation and prepares users to understand the challenges of future human exploration. The proposed technical architecture incorporates HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript for the user interface and interactive functionality. Python can support scientific calculations and mission modelling, while Three.js can provide three-dimensional visualisations of spacecraft, planets and exploration environments. NASA's publicly available datasets can provide scientific information for more realistic simulations. Artificial intelligence could also support mission analysis, risk identification and decision-making. The platform is designed for computers and mobile devices without requiring specialised physical hardware. MissionVariessi is creative because it allows users to become virtual mission controllers rather than passive observers of space exploration. Through interactive simulations, users can investigate questions such as what happens when astronauts run low on oxygen or when a spacecraft loses communication with Earth. Its combination of scientific information, interactive 3D environments and scenario-based learning creates an engaging educational experience. During development, HONGIE MIGUEL TEAM considered scientific accuracy, astronaut safety, environmental differences between the Moon and Mars, communication delays, resource availability, accessibility, scalability and technological limitations. We recognise that realistic mission simulation requires reliable scientific data and clearly defined assumptions. Our vision is to make space exploration more accessible, interactive and inspiring. MISSIONVARIESSI: Plan the Mission. Simulate the Challenges. Explore Beyond Earth.
